clue.text: Maybe arse wants gold provided – and diamonds

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
provided that = on condition = if
ice is old underworld slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A crude image of a backside craving gold and diamonds, the Eye mocking bling-hungry greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' simply joins the last piece on. 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: the backside is one instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear end is one example of a bodily opening, hence the 'maybe' signalling an instance rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Presenter who went too far in one (he scored)

blocks.note: Jonathan Ross, the TV and radio host suspended in 2008 over lewd prank calls to actor Andrew Sachs
used literally
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster who overstepped the mark, and who (the aside hints) had sexual success too.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a smutty aside about the presenter, but 'scored' is musical: the composer wrote scores.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer of The Barber of Seville wrote music, and writing orchestral music is scoring it.

clue.text: Almighty brown trouser moment for those you put it into?

definitions.text: Almighty brown trouser moment for those you put it into?

blocks.note: surface reading: a huge moment of terror, the kind that soils your trousers

blocks.clueFragment: for those you put it into?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the idiom where you 'put' this dread into someone, with 'Almighty' pointing at the deity

explanation.surface: A vulgar picture of someone so frightened they soil themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almighty' works twice: as the slang intensifier (an almighty fright) and as the name of the deity in the phrase. A 'brown trouser moment' is British slang for a terrifying moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To put this into someone is the idiom for terrifying them, so it is the terror felt by its recipients.

clue.text: The bloke's surrounded by court tits

indicators.note: something with others all round it sits inside them

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation of court
the bloke's = he's, he is

explanation.surface: A tabloid image of a man in court surrounded by topless women, or by fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tits' tempts as idiots or as birds; it is the definition, meaning breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for breasts stands for the front of the torso, the bust area in general.

clue.text: "Humble" party does a U-turn inside minute (Clegg's third way)

indicators.note: one piece placed within another is inside it
turning round to face the opposite direction means reading backwards
an ordinal picks out a single letter by its position

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for minute
a do is a party
the third letter of the Lib Dem leader's name
St, street, a way

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg's Liberal Democrats, pitching a humble third way, reverse a policy in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed party sits inside M...EST, formed from the minute plus Clegg's third letter and the way. Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, Britain's third party, in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unassuming and not boastful is what both words describe; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: This woman's top affected March air outside temperature

indicators.note: something affected has been altered from its natural state
letters on the outside wrap round what is within

blocks.note: anagram fodder
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A woman's top reacting to the chilly March weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like clothing, a blouse in cold weather; it means top person, and 'This woman's' makes that person female.
explanation.definitionFit: The female head of a family or group is the woman at the top of it.

clue.text: Get pants off and have sex, mounted, with Silver

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means going upwards, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to bed someone is to have sex with them
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A bawdy scene of undressing and sex in the saddle, perhaps with the Lone Ranger's horse, Silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' plays on the sexual position and on a rider on horseback, but it is the reversal instruction for a down light. 'With' just joins the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This British schoolboy slang means stripping someone of their trousers, which Britons call pants, as a prank.

clue.text: 8 down's minute parts

blocks.note: what a double helping of food consists of: going back for more
sixty of these make up a minute

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking for the small components of another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is a double helping, so the first sense is second helpings; 'minute' looks like 'tiny' but is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Second helpings of food and the sixty divisions of a minute share this one plural word.

clue.text: A Prescott treat is what Eye readers got in the case of Crossword 402

definitions.text: what Eye readers got in the case of Crossword 402

blocks.note: John Prescott, the Labour deputy prime minister, was mocked for his large appetite

blocks.clueFragment: what Eye readers got in the case of Crossword 402
blocks.note: a reference to something about that earlier Private Eye puzzle which gave readers twice as much

explanation.surface: An in-joke to Private Eye readers about a past crossword, tied to a jibe at a greedy politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense relies on Prescott's reputation as a big eater. The second refers to Crossword 402, which evidently gave readers a doubled serving; exactly what happened to it is not recoverable from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A second portion piled on is what a greedy eater relishes, and a doubled crossword serving is the same idea.

clue.text: What blundering minister seeks? Neo-gestapo suppressing state

indicators.note: neo means new, and a new version of the letters is a rearrangement
to suppress is to hold down, keeping something held within

blocks.note: anagram fodder
CA is the abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A modern secret police force crushing the state, set beside a minister looking for a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neo-gestapo' reads as a single word for a new secret police; the prefix is split off as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister who has blundered looks for someone else to take the blame, a person made to carry others' faults.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Reviled copper, openly gay, makes you scoff

blocks.note: pig is a derogatory slang word for a police officer
someone out has publicly declared being gay

explanation.surface: A despised policeman coming out as gay provokes scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' reads as sneer, the reaction to the story; it means eat greedily, British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge greedily on food is the British slang sense of scoffing, a verb for eating fast.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Bingo! Darling fixed a "tiding over" advance

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or altered, its order tampered with

blocks.note: anagram fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: Chancellor Alistair Darling triumphantly rigging a stopgap loan during the 2008 banking crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Darling was the British Chancellor of the Exchequer who propped up the banks; here his name is just letters. The answer runs on into 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-term money that covers a gap until longer finance arrives is exactly a loan meant to tide someone over.

clue.text: Jeremy Clarkson's gay? Gee, bring out the queen!

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as in a sum being out

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An exclamation of mock surprise at the macho TV presenter being gay, then a camp cry to bring on the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring' serves as fodder and nothing else; 'Clarkson' is the Top Gear host known for politically incorrect jokes, the sort who would use this slang. Ginger beer is Cockney rhyming slang: it rhymes with queer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is rhyming slang for homosexual, the kind of laddish euphemism the blokey motoring presenter might use.

clue.text: They wouldn't keep an artist in residence

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits within it

blocks.note: res. is the abbreviation for residence
J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: Someone who would not house an artist in residence, as a gallery or college might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist in residence' reads as a single job title; it has to be split into the painter and the abbreviation that holds him.
explanation.definitionFit: People who send goods back rather than holding on to them are those who give things back.

clue.text: see 21dn.
What's in store for the barren old goat, really?

definitions.text: What's in store for the barren old goat

blocks.clueFragment: What's in store for the barren old goat
blocks.note: a young goat is a kid, and an infertile nanny will bear none
the incredulous exclamation of disbelief

explanation.surface: A mock-sympathetic question about a lecherous old man, an 'old goat', unable to father children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old goat' suggests a randy old man; read literally, kidding is a goat giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in surprise, the phrase asks whether someone is serious, the same as asking whether something is genuinely so.

clue.text: (& 10ac.) Screwed rugby player and relaxed

blocks.note: slang for having had sex
one of the rugby positions behind the scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player unwinding after sex, or after being cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed' could mean cheated; here it is the sexual sense. The answer runs on into 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going, unhurried manner is what it means to be calm and at ease.

clue.text: A Labour about to ditch union leader for one, is mostly OPEC's concern

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so this takes the opening letter
to ditch is to discard, throwing something out to make room
for here means in place of, swapping one thing in where another was
about signals moving things round into another order

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the swap
the leading letter of union, the one to ditch
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Labour government, ready to drop a union boss, worrying about what concerns the oil cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' reads as a trade union boss, apt for Labour, but it is only the letter to be replaced. OPEC is the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Much of what the petroleum exporters' cartel controls is Middle Eastern crude, hence 'mostly'.

clue.text: Formalise the relationship between two bondage freaks?

blocks.note: to marry, making a partnership official
read literally: what rope enthusiasts would do, binding someone

explanation.surface: A couple who are into being tied up deciding to make it official.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for marrying is read literally, as what fans of restraint do with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means getting married, making a couple's partnership formal and legal.

clue.text: Pentagon taking sides when Obama's chief can't go bombing?

indicators.note: the chief part of a word is its head, its leading letter
something bombed is blown apart and its pieces scattered

blocks.note: the initial of the US president's name
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The US defence headquarters picking sides when the President refuses to authorise air strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking sides' looks like partisanship; it means acquiring more sides, which turns a five-sided figure into an eight-sided one.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided figure that acquires three more edges becomes the eight-sided polygon.

clue.text: Broadcast by King George being gobbled by cool lock-keeper?

indicators.note: whatever is gobbled ends up inside the one eating it

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
GR, Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A royal broadcast swallowed up by a trendy canal lock-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-keeper' suggests a canal worker; a lock is also a strand of hair, and this clip keeps it in place. A hairgrip is British for a bobby pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sprung clip holds a strand of hair in place, so it literally keeps a lock.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) It's not giving up sex and punctuation produces such a discharging organ

blocks.clueFragment: It's not giving up sex and punctuation
blocks.note: surface reading: someone refusing to abandon sex or careful punctuation
setter's reading: the organ that streams mucus when you have a cold

explanation.surface: A mock-serious remark that clinging to sex and punctuation leads to an organ that discharges.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 15 across. 'Discharging organ' suggests something sexual; it is the nose streaming with a cold. How the first half yields the answer is not fully clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose streaming with mucus during a cold is an organ that discharges fluid.

clue.text: Balls caught in revolving seat? Calm down!

indicators.note: something caught in a net ends up enclosed by it
revolving turns things round, shifting their order

blocks.note: Ed Balls, the Labour cabinet minister in 2009
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone telling a man whose testicles are trapped in a swivel chair to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is the politician Ed Balls, not anatomy; his first name is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone, especially with a drug, is the verb here, matching the imperative.

clue.text: Certainly not pissed off, Boers

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, not in its proper state

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Annoyed South African farmers, the Boers, who are 'pissed off'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed off' reads as one phrase meaning annoyed; it splits, with 'pissed' (British for drunk) in the definition and 'off' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Not being drunk at all is the plain meaning, since pissed is British slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Creating peers? (None organised before show of wealth)

indicators.note: to organise is to put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder
bling is flashy jewellery flaunting wealth

explanation.surface: A dig at honours for rich donors, with 'show of wealth' coming before any ennoblement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' could be equals; here they are members of the House of Lords, which the Eye implies money buys.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising people to the nobility makes them lords, members of the British upper house.

clue.text: Dolly's bust: it had a number of  unfortunate names

definitions.text: it had a number of  unfortunate names

indicators.note: something bust is broken, its parts in disarray

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Dolly Parton's famous bust, which acquired a lot of unkind nicknames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a bosom; it is the instruction. The Names were the private investors behind Lloyd's of London, the insurance market, many of whom were ruined by huge claims around 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: The London insurance market's backers are called Names, and many suffered catastrophic losses, making them unlucky.

clue.text: Pathetic prey, Gordon, having no right party issue

indicators.note: having none of something means it has been taken away
pathetic means feeble, falling apart and in a poor state

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the name before losing its letters
R is the abbreviation for right
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Prime Minister Gordon Brown as feeble prey, lacking a right-wing party line on some issue.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the R and the DO from the name leaves GON, which joins the prey in the anagram. 'Issue' looks like a political question but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring or descendants are someone's issue, in the old legal sense of children.
